hints: Determine the maximum speed reached by the car at the end of the accelerating stage using $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$, $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 10\text{ s}$.
Identify the key time coordinates for the stages: accelerating from $t = 0$ to $t = 10$, constant speed for 30 s until $t = 40$, and decelerating to rest over 20 s until $t = 60$.

Sketch a single trapezium starting at the origin $(0,0)$, rising to $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 10\text{ s}$, staying horizontal until $t = 40\text{ s}$, and sloping downwards to meet the time axis at $t = 60\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the peak speed reached by the car during the acceleration stage using $v = u + at$:
$$v = 0 + 2 \times 10 = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine the key times for the motion stages:
$$\text{Accelerating phase: } t = 0\text{ to } t = 10\text{ s}$$
$$\text{Constant-speed phase: } t = 10\text{ to } t = 10 + 30 = 40\text{ s}$$
$$\text{Decelerating phase: } t = 40\text{ to } t = 40 + 20 = 60\text{ s}$$

Sketch a trapezoidal velocity-time graph on the positive axes starting at $(0,0)$, with a straight line increasing to $(10, 20)$, a horizontal segment from $(10, 20)$ to $(40, 20)$, and a straight line decreasing to $(60, 0)$. Clearly label $20$ on the vertical velocity axis, and $10$, $40$, and $60$ on the horizontal time axis.
teacher_walkthrough: First, let us find the peak velocity achieved by the car. The car starts from rest, which means its initial velocity is $u = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It accelerates at a constant rate $a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ for a time duration $t = 10\text{ s}$.

State the constant-acceleration formula linking velocity, acceleration, and time:
$$v = u + at$$

Substitute the values $u = 0$, $a = 2$, and $t = 10$:
$$v = 0 + (2)(10) = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Next, determine the timeline along the horizontal $t$-axis for each phase of the journey:
1. Acceleration phase: starts at $t = 0\text{ s}$ and ends at $t = 10\text{ s}$. The velocity increases linearly from $0$ to $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

2. Constant-speed phase: the car maintains this speed of $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $30\text{ s}$. The time at the end of this phase is:
$$t_2 = 10 + 30 = 40\text{ s}$$

3. Deceleration phase: the car decelerates uniformly to rest over a period of $20\text{ s}$. The time when it comes to rest is:
$$t_3 = 40 + 20 = 60\text{ s}$$

Now sketch the velocity-time graph: draw a horizontal $t$-axis and a vertical $v$-axis. From $(0,0)$, draw a straight line of positive gradient up to the point $(10, 20)$. From $(10, 20)$, draw a horizontal line segment to $(40, 20)$. From $(40, 20)$, draw a straight line of negative gradient down to $(60, 0)$ on the time axis. Clearly label the peak value $20$ on the vertical axis, and the time values $10$, $40$, and $60$ on the horizontal axis.

hints: Recall that on a velocity-time graph, the total distance travelled equals the total area between the velocity curve and the time axis.
Use the formula for the area of a trapezium: $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$, where $a$ and $b$ are the lengths of the parallel sides and $h$ is the perpendicular height.
Substitute the parallel side lengths $a = 40 - 10 = 30\text{ s}$, $b = 60\text{ s}$, and height $h = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the area formula.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total distance from the area under the velocity-time graph using the area of a trapezium formula:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$$

Identify the dimensions of the trapezium:
$$a = 40 - 10 = 30\text{ s},\quad b = 60 - 0 = 60\text{ s},\quad h = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall the fundamental geometric principle for velocity-time graphs: the total distance travelled by a moving particle is given by the area under its velocity-time graph between the initial and final times:
$$\text{Distance} = \text{Area under } v\text{-}t \text{ graph}$$
The shape of the graph sketched in part (a) is a trapezium with two horizontal parallel edges:

The top parallel edge corresponds to the constant-speed interval from $t = 10\text{ s}$ to $t = 40\text{ s}$, which has length:
$$a = 40 - 10 = 30\text{ s}$$

The bottom parallel edge along the time axis runs from $t = 0\text{ s}$ to $t = 60\text{ s}$, which has length:
$$b = 60 - 0 = 60\text{ s}$$

The perpendicular height between the parallel edges is the peak speed:
$$h = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Write down the standard formula for the area of a trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h$$

Substitute the dimensions into the formula:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(30 + 60)(20)$$

Perform the intermediate arithmetic calculations:
$$30 + 60 = 90$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 90 \times 20 = 90 \times 10 = 900\text{ m}$$
Therefore, the total distance travelled by the car is $900\text{ m}$.
